newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends slightly down, but off early lows.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends slightly down, but off early lows.

text.p: NWE naphtha was mildly weaker on Thursday having been talked considerably lower for most of the day only to recover slightly on crude futures and related gasoline gains, traders said.

Naphtha swaps for April were talked around the $204/$206 cif NWE level in early trade but players said they were beginning to look a bit more healthy by the end of the day in line with gasoline gains.

Some traders attributed the earlier weakness to an apparent lack of end-user demand amid healthy supply, while others said the losses had been forced on the market by players working the East/West spread.
The East/West spread has opened out to the $30 per tonne range over the past week having been as narrow as $23 two weeks ago, traders said.
"They want to keep the spread as wide as possible," said one trader.
Traders said a cargo offered out of the U.K. appeared to have been put back into storage after the seller failed to get high enough bids.
Some players suggested, however, that the offering of the cargo had been a ruse to keep NWE prices as low as possible while the player priced a cargo it was buying out of Skikda.
